description.narrative:
The impact of the Project is improved health status and quality of life for the population of Mongolia. The outcome of the Project is PHC services that are more effective and improved financial protection through health insurance.
The Project has four components designed through collaboration and coordination with key stakeholders in the health sector.
1. Strengthened Health Services: (i) sustainable and institutionalized FGPs, (ii) Soum health centers with improved infrastructure, (iii) district and aimag general hospitals supporting FGPs and SHCs
2. Improved Health Care Financing and Health Insurance: (i) health resource allocation and purchasing, (ii) strengthened health insurance to improve financial protection and expand coverage, (iii) improved hospital financial efficiency through governance and incentives.
3. Improved Human Resources Development: (i) improved health HR management and capacity, (ii) incentives and motivation schemes to improve rural health care.
4. Sector capacity development and management: (i) increased capacity of MOH and key agencies to implement the HSMO, (ii) improved governance in the health sector, (iii) private sector development policy and guidelines established, (iv) project management capacity enhanced.

Output: Output 1. Strengthened family group practices (FGPs) as the first level of primary health care (PHC) Indicator: Policy recommendations on legal, tax, business, and social status of FGP approved by Government Progress/Status: The recommendations of FGPs legal status have been introduced to the Ministerial Counsel at MOH and an official decision was made to keep the current status of FGPs as private entity. In addition, relevant policy papers, and laws were identified that need to be modified in accordance with this decision. MOH incorporated the recommendations into new amendment to Health law which was submitted in July 2010 to the Parliament for discussion.
The new Health law (passed in May 2011) reflected major reforms planned under the THSDP; (a) legal status of FGPs (as private entities), (b) definition of FGPs and care provided by FGPs, (c) voluntary enrollment, (d) contract based financing, (e) use of state/local assets free of charge, (f) incentive package for FGP staff. FGPs standard was discussed and approved by the health service standard committee by the MOH. The standard is approved by National Office of Standard and Measurement in Feb 2011. The standard reflected FGPs current legal status, and strengthening the practice as a gate keeper in the future. FGPs performance indicators were reviewed and revised as a part of performance contract revision;
FGP performance contract, performance criteria and evaluation, voluntary enrollment, number of residents to be attached to FGP clinic, per-capita financing, additional financing for serving non-registered/migrant people, use and maintenance of facilities are incorporated into Bylaw on FGPs, which is approved by Cabinet in Dec 2011 (Government resolution #364, 2011).
MOH endorsed the "Midterm strategy on reform of the Family health center's services" in June 2013. Data Source: Cabinet/Government order(s) Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Target year: 2012 Target value: Y

Policy and guidelines on private sector development and regulation in health established and operational Indicator: Regulatory framework for private health sector operations, financing, licensing, and monitoring in place Progress/Status: The project developed report on Licensing and regulatory framework for healthcare facilities with focus on private sector. The report includes a review of current situation and recommendation on (1) reforming existing framework with clear definition of a Purpose and overall Objective of the licensing, (2) applying uniform licensing requirements, (3) linking license requirements with the service packages, and (4) introducing the Certificate of need tool. The report was approved by the PCS first in Nov 2011. Main recommendations were adopted in revised Ministerial order on licensing regulation issued in June 2012. The newly established PSC requested the project to re-visit the recommendations, and re-discussed the report in March 2012. In April 2014, MOH revised (i) the regulation on licensing of private hospitals (order #145, 2013); and (ii) regulation on licensing committee, term and references (order #143, 2013). The review includes also recommendations on general approaches to out of pocket payments, co-payments and payment methods. It is proposed to lay down the principles and procedures for determining the benefits package, including the out of pocket payments and provider payment systems in the law and to create flexibility in yearly amending these in accordance with felt needs via implementation regulations like decrees, resolutions and ministerial orders, based on the law.
Some recommendations are incorporated in the draft amended health insurance law and submitted to Parliament in June 2010. These include (i) family enrolment, (ii) increasing government subsidies for poor (iii) introducing government subsidy for informal sector, and (iv) increasing benefit package. The law is awaiting the further discussion by the Parliament.
